comparison: Both address claims C11-C14 about Ptpmt1 knockout validation and developmental phenotypes. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by qRT-PCR and observational data, noting C14 requires longer-term assessment. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 explicitly challenging that developmental effects have been ruled out, demanding 'detailed developmental assessment by histology at various developmental stages' and noting that 'many developmental issues progress over time and manifest later in adulthood.'

OpenEval addresses C15-C19 (muscle atrophy progression), finding them well-supported by multiple lines of evidence. Peer R2 addresses broader phenotypic claims C15-C30 including functional deficits. Peer review finds these SUPPORTED, with reviewers acknowledging 'solid methodology' and that metabolic inflexibility leads to muscular atrophy, though Reviewer 3 notes 'most of the data lack quantification.'

OpenEval addresses C20-C23 (functional muscle impairments), finding them SUPPORTED by wire hang and treadmill tests. These claims overlap with peer R2's broader coverage of C15-C30. Peer review finds the phenotypic observations SUPPORTED despite quantification concerns.

OpenEval addresses C24-C30 (ex vivo force measurements and muscle fiber observations), finding them SUPPORTED. These overlap with peer R2's coverage of C15-C30. Peer review acknowledges the phenotypic data as SUPPORTED with 'solid methodology.'

OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by measurements and expression analysis, noting C40-C41 inferences would benefit from direct mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation measurement.
